opinions.rationale: The claim is internally consistent and correctly scoped as a problem of current practice (lack of standardization and integration) rather than a structural impossibility. The reasons given for it being open (incompatible identification stories, untestable assumptions differing across tools) genuinely support the claim that these tools are not currently integrated into a standard emulation workflow. The severity is proportionate to the methodological gap.

The claim is internally consistent and correctly scoped as a gap in current practice and available theory rather than a structural impossibility. The reasons given for it being open (bias parameters living on different scales, non-product joint regions due to interactions, and professional costs) genuinely support the claim that joint sensitivity analyses are not standard and lack established, convenient theory. The severity is proportionate to the methodological gap.
